title: Writing: A Reflective Essay on Communication Skills

writingModel.placeholder: Identify the communication skill you will reflect on and why it matters
writingModel.hint: "Effective X is essential for… / One of the most significant challenges I face as a communicator is…"

writingModel.placeholder: Describe your current strengths and weaknesses in this area
writingModel.hint: Be specific and honest — use "I tend to…", "I often find…", "My greatest strength is…"

writingModel.placeholder: Analyse why you have these patterns — background, experience, cultural context
writingModel.hint: "This is partly because…" / "Growing up in a high-context culture, I tend to…"

writingModel.placeholder: Describe specific steps you will take to improve
writingModel.hint: "With a view to improving X, I intend to…" / "I will practise Y in low-stakes situations…"

writingModel.placeholder: Draw a broader conclusion about the value of communication skills
writingModel.hint: "In the interests of becoming a more effective communicator, I recognise that…"

writingTemplate.prefix: Of the many skills required for effective communication, I find
writingTemplate.placeholder: active listening in high-stakes professional contexts
writingTemplate.hint: Open with a specific, honest identification of the challenge

writingTemplate.placeholder: I am generally good at signposting my ideas clearly / I tend to rush when nervous

writingTemplate.prefix: This pattern is partly explained by
writingTemplate.placeholder: my background in a high-context culture, where explicit verbal signposting is less common
writingTemplate.hint: Analyse the cultural or personal roots of your patterns

writingTemplate.prefix: With a view to improving, I intend to
writingTemplate.suffix: in low-stakes situations first, before applying the same strategy under pressure.
writingTemplate.placeholder: practise deliberate pausing and eye contact during casual conversations
writingTemplate.hint: "With a view to + gerund" + low-stakes practice strategy

writingTemplate.prefix: In the interests of becoming a genuinely effective communicator, I recognise that
writingTemplate.placeholder: improvement requires not just practice but the willingness to reflect honestly on failure
writingTemplate.hint: "In the interests of + noun" = formal purposive phrase

items: I tend to rush when I am nervous or uncertain.
I find it difficult to maintain eye contact under pressure.
My greatest challenge as a listener is maintaining concentration over long periods.
I often use fillers rather than pausing deliberately.
I have a tendency to assume my listeners are following me.
This pattern is partly explained by my cultural background.
Growing up in a high-context culture, I am accustomed to leaving things unsaid.
My instinct to rush is, I believe, a consequence of anxiety about judgement.
The tendency to over-explain is common in academic contexts.
This habit was reinforced by years of formal education in a particular style.
With a view to improving my pacing, I will practise deliberate pausing.
In the interests of becoming a clearer communicator, I will focus on signposting.
I intend to practise repair strategies in low-stakes conversations first.
By recording myself, I will be able to identify patterns I am not consciously aware of.
I will seek feedback from trusted colleagues on specific aspects of my delivery.
Effective communication is, arguably, the most important professional skill.
Good listening is a gift to the person being listened to.
Communicative intelligence develops over time through practice and reflection.
The willingness to be uncomfortable is a prerequisite for genuine development.
In the interests of effective cross-cultural communication, I must hold my interpretations tentatively.

questions.text: "You've thought carefully about your communication style, ___?" (tag)
questions.hint: Positive + present perfect → negative tag "haven't you"

questions.text: "I don't practise signposting enough in casual conversation, ___ ___?" (tag)
"___, I'm not sure I've been listening actively enough." (signalling honesty)
"___ ___ ___ improving my listening, I will practise in low-stakes conversations first." (with the aim of)
questions.hint: "With a view to + gerund" = with the aim of

questions.text: "___ effective communication, I recognise that practice and reflection are both essential." (for the benefit of)
questions.hint: "In the interests of + noun/gerund" = for the benefit of

questions.text: "This is kind of difficult to explain" uses a hedge appropriately in informal reflection.
questions.hint: "Kind of" = informal hedge — appropriate in personal reflective writing
Positive past simple → negative tag "didn't she"

questions.text: "___, the key insight is this: communication repair matters more than linguistic accuracy." (summarising)
questions.hint: "Basically" = getting to the core point / summarising
